Done. The export passed on the first execution.

**What I built:** `out/T3/solution.py`, a plain torch plus safetensors script. It matches the 64 projection matrices with an anchored regex, casts them to bfloat16, drops the 48 attention buffers by name, and upcasts everything else to float32. The four required checks run before any file is written and exit non-zero on failure. Tensors are then packed greedily in key order under the 256 MiB budget, written as nine shards with an index file, and re-read to verify bit-exact values.

**Output in `out/T3/`:**

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Tensors | 196 (64 bfloat16, 132 float32) |
| Shards | 9, embeddings alone in shards 1 and 2 |
| Total tensor bytes | 2,436,513,792 |

**One note:** the task quotes the embeddings as 206 MB, which is their float16 size. After the mandated float32 upcast they are 412 MB each, so they still sit alone in their own shards as the rules require.

`out/T3/REPORT.md` holds the self-report, including why I chose a script over `transformers.save_pretrained`, which forces a single dtype and re-creates rotary buffers.
